research_concepts: play-type possession records derived from play-by-play
methodological_questions: Can role portability be tested with n=24 units?
How should portability be measured across seasons or regular season versus playoffs?
What sample size and power are needed to compare two play-style groups?
How reliable are play-type labels derived from play-by-play?
Are usage, minutes, and lineup context confounding the cut-versus-drive contrast?

historical_evidence.finding: In 92 connector movers, pre-move cut share predicted whether connector function reproduced after a move (rho +0.265, LOO AUC 0.622, permutation p=0.005; holds when dropping Gafford). The record calls this exploratory, notes that almost all other pre-move predictors were null, and says the paper treats cut share as a boundary condition. Its sample is connector movers defined by organizational function, not NBA play-type shapers in the 2022-23 to 2025-26 data.

Tested whether matching a mover's initiation diet to a destination's thin jobs predicts post-move outcomes. Of 198 movers, 19 were taxonomy connectors and the 15.7% match rate left 5 matched connectors. The all-movers binary result (p=0.0283) did not hold as a continuous Spearman (-0.034). Connector-specific delta match was +0.540 vs +0.069 (p=0.156, n=5/14). Recorded verdict: null.

Tested DRIVE-as-BEST counters against a feasibility-constrained play-type mix on 44 triggers from 13 teams. Observed gap was -0.066 (p=0.2175 vs B_fixed). Minimum detectable effect at 80% power was about 0.180 PPP (SD about 0.34), so a null and an effect up to 0.18 PPP could not be distinguished.

Archived check of whether mover portability relates to destination net-rating change. Recorded as 'underpowered and null once corrected for landing-spot quality'. No numbers were kept, and it was dropped from Paper 1. Its failure type is recorded as A_unanswerable.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Binary diet-to-destination match on connector subsets, with an all-movers binary test and a continuous Spearman follow-up.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as LIM:small_sample. Only 19 taxonomy connectors and 5 matched connectors remained after matching. The all-movers binary result did not replicate as a continuous Spearman, so the connector-specific test was not licensed.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Counter-effect test of DRIVE-as-BEST triggers against a constrained play-type mix.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as LIM:low_power_large_MDE and LIM:small_sample. With n=44 the observed gap was below the MDE of 0.180 PPP, so the null is uninformative.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Mover portability versus destination net-rating change.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as LIM:low_power_large_MDE and LIM:small_sample, stated as underpowered and requiring a landing-spot correction. No numbers were kept, so the result cannot be checked.

evidence_establishes: Earlier project work has tested cut-versus-drive and play-type portability questions only on small or differently defined samples: 92 connector movers in FAM:SF-CHT-057, 19 taxonomy connectors in FAM:SF-APPS-090, 44 triggers in FAM:SF-APPS-024, and an unreported archive check in FAM:SF-PAP-029.

Small-sample comparisons of this kind have repeatedly been underpowered or unlicensed. FAM:SF-APPS-024 and FAM:SF-PAP-029 record low power, and FAM:SF-APPS-090 records a binary result that did not survive a continuous test.

FAM:SF-CHT-057 is the only retrieved record with a positive cut-share portability signal. It is exploratory, its sample is connector movers rather than the 24 shaper units, and it reports cut share as a boundary condition rather than a general effect.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests cut-heavy versus drive-heavy NBA shapers using 2022-23 to 2025-26 play-by-play-derived possession records.

No retrieved record shows that cut share predicts role portability for shapers. FAM:SF-CHT-057 is about connectors moving between organizations, and the cut-share result may not transfer to shaper roles or to within-team or playoff contexts.
No retrieved record gives a usable power calculation for n=24 units. FAM:SF-PAP-029 kept no numbers, and FAM:SF-APPS-024 gives an MDE for n=44 only.
The retrieved records do not show whether portability is defined as reproduction across seasons, teams, or regular season versus playoffs, so the outcome definition cannot be checked against them.
own_inferences: With n=24 split into two groups of about 12, a two-sample comparison at alpha 0.05 and 80% power can only detect a very large standardized difference (roughly d of 1.2 or more). This is my calculation, not a retrieved result.

A cut-versus-drive contrast on 24 units is likely to be confounded by usage, minutes, position, and team context, and possibly by the play-type label itself, since portability may be measured with the same possession data that defines cut and drive shares.
If the question is kept, a defensible test needs more units, such as player-season or player-context observations, than the 24 recorded units. Otherwise the result would be descriptive.
uncertainties: The unit count of 24 is recorded as 'units available to a study of this question' and may not be the same as player-seasons, so the true sample for a shaper-level test is not known.

Portability has no defined operational outcome in the task statement. Candidates include reproduction of cut or drive share across seasons, team changes, or regular season versus playoffs, and each would need a separate definition.
Play-type labels are derived from play-by-play in a graph database. Their reliability for cut versus drive classification is not reported in the retrieved material.

FAM:SF-CHT-057 has a status of supported, but the record calls it exploratory and reports p=0.011 in one place and a permutation p=0.005 in another. Its sample and definition differ from the present question.
The archived record FAM:SF-PAP-029 has no numbers, so its effect size cannot be used.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records show that comparable small-sample tests in this project were underpowered, unlicensed, or untestable (FAM:SF-APPS-024, FAM:SF-APPS-090, FAM:SF-PAP-029). Together with the exploratory, differently defined FAM:SF-CHT-057 signal, this moved the decision from a provisional proceed toward do_not_proceed as a confirmatory test on 24 units. The historical evidence does not show the question is unanswerable in principle, so the recommended path is a descriptive analysis or a redesigned study with more units.

blocking_constraints.text: With 24 units, only very large group differences are detectable. FAM:SF-APPS-024 and FAM:SF-PAP-029 record the same low-power problem in comparable settings.
Cut and drive shares come from derived play-type labels, and their reliability and portability measure are not established in the retrieved records.
Usage, minutes, position, lineup, and team context may drive both play style and any observed portability, and the 24-unit sample cannot adjust for them adequately.

prior_work.summary: Earlier project work has examined related questions on connector movers and drive-versus-cut play types. FAM:SF-CHT-057 reports a supported but exploratory cut-share effect in 92 connector movers, with the paper treating it as a boundary condition. FAM:SF-APPS-090, FAM:SF-APPS-024, and FAM:SF-PAP-029 are untestable or underpowered in small samples. None of these tests cut-heavy versus drive-heavy NBA shapers in the 2022-23 to 2025-26 data with 24 units, so the question is only partly answered by prior work and is not answered for this sample.

risks.text: n=24 gives very low power for a two-group comparison, and a null would be uninformative about moderate effects.
Cut-heavy and drive-heavy classifications depend on derived play-type labels whose reliability is unknown.
If portability is defined from the same possession-level play-type data, the outcome and the predictor may share a label, which inflates apparent portability.
Usage, minutes, role on team, and lineup context may account for both play style and portability differences.
Seasons from 2022-23 to 2025-26 and regular season versus playoffs may differ in play style and role transfer, so pooled portability estimates may mix contexts.
Choosing among several portability definitions, play-type cutoffs, and subgroups would inflate false positives unless the primary contrast is fixed in advance.
Possession attribution and initiator assignment from play-by-play may misclassify cut and drive possessions.

design.estimand: Difference in portability between cut-heavy and drive-heavy shapers, where portability is a pre-specified measure of how far a shaper's role reproduces across a context change (for example, regular season to playoffs or season to season). The question as posed does not define the outcome, so this estimand must be fixed before any run.
design.unit: Player-season (or player-context) shaper observation, not the team or the 24 recorded units unless those are confirmed to be shaper-level.
design.sample: The 24 units as recorded from NBA 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons and playoffs, used only for a descriptive pilot. A confirmatory test would need more units, and the minimum sample must be set from a power calculation before data are read.
design.power: At n=24 (about 12 per group) only a very large standardized difference (d of about 1.2 or more) is detectable at alpha 0.05 and 80% power (own calculation). Any confirmatory claim requires a pre-registered MDE and a sample that reaches it; otherwise the result is reported as descriptive.
design.controls: Adjust for minutes, usage rate, position, team and lineup context, and season. Use a derived-label reliability check (for example, split-half or inter-coder agreement on a sample of possessions) before classifying shapers as cut-heavy or drive-heavy. Do not use the outcome to define the labels.
design.falsification: Permutation test of cut-share labels against the portability outcome (as in FAM:SF-CHT-057), plus a placebo contrast using a non-play-style trait. Expect the placebo to be null; a non-null placebo signals confounding or label leakage.
design.multiplicity: One pre-specified primary contrast (cut-heavy minus drive-heavy portability under one fixed definition). All other definitions, subgroups, and cutoffs are secondary and corrected with Holm, or reported as exploratory.
design.decision_rule: Claim support only if the primary contrast is significant at the pre-specified alpha after the fixed controls, the effect exceeds the pre-registered MDE, the label-reliability check passes, and the placebo is null. If the sample does not reach the MDE, report the result as inconclusive and do not claim rejection.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23, 2023-24, and 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs, and 2025-26 regular season and playoffs as complete on 2026-08-08 (regular season complete from 2026-04-13; playoffs complete from 2026-06-21). Freeze the data version before analysis.

methodological_questions: can role transfer or portability be tested with n=24 units
how to measure role portability across seasons or playoffs
sample size and power for comparing two play-style groups
measurement reliability of play-type classifications derived from play-by-play
confounding by usage, minutes, and lineup context
args.query: Do cut-heavy shapers' structural roles travel (generalize or transfer across contexts) better than drive-heavy shapers' roles? Prior studies on role portability, play-type derived labels, and small-sample NBA role analyses.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

messages.content:
Research question (as posed on 2026-08-08, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=24

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
